submissions.title: Memphis Data Center Temporary Moratorium Ordinance (v3)
submissions.excerpt: Shall not process, schedule, hear, approve, or issue any approval
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Memphis City Council ordinance imposing a 12-month moratorium on new data-center zoning, site-plan, and building-permit approvals city-wide; third/final reading was on the council's agenda for 2026-10-06 (per the council's own meeting calendar, https://memphistn.gov/event/city-council-board-meeting-2/2026-10-06/, and Hoodline's 2026-10 preview 'Memphis Council Faces Final Vote on Data Center Pause as Rally Targets Musk'). Second reading passed unanimously 2026-09-01. The ordinance explicitly exempts xAI's existing Memphis facilities (tracked project xAI Colossus 2, status UNDER_CONSTRUCTION, within Memphis city limits) — it would only block NEW data-center approvals, not the tracked site. I could not confirm the outcome of the 2026-10-06 final vote in sources available to this search (coverage of that specific session had not yet been indexed) — please verify whether it passed before treating the moratorium as in force.

submissions.title: NV Energy sues Tract over cost allocation for Reno-area data center campuses
submissions.excerpt: Large-load customers should bear the costs required to serve their projects and should not shift those costs onto Nevada families
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION / utility dispute: NV Energy sued data-center developer Tract (doing business locally as Fleet Data Centers) in Washoe County district court on 2026-08-07 over who pays for grid upgrades serving two planned Reno-area campuses, which press reports say 'could draw more than 2 GW' combined (site power, not IT load, and not confirmed by either party in terms I could verify directly) -- versus a separately reported standalone Tract/Fleet Reno project sized at 230 MW utility capacity / 200 MW critical IT load. CBS News and other outlets call this the first lawsuit by a major utility against a data-center developer over cost-shifting. No Nevada or Washoe County project currently exists in the tracker (I searched for 'Tract', 'Reno', 'Nevada', 'Washoe' in project names/owners/locations and found none), so this is a new-project candidate as well as a restriction/dispute record. This is dated five weeks before my search window and the agent has no way to confirm it hasn't already been reviewed and declined -- flagging as potentially already seen.

claims.methodology: Press paraphrase of utility's court filing describing combined draw of two planned campuses as 'more than 2 GW'; not a direct quote and not confirmed by Tract
